graph.summary: Metformin → 5'-AMP-activated protein kinase catalytic subunit alpha-1 → gluconeogenesis → Hyperglycemia → Diabetes mellitus type 2

evidence.snippet: activation of AMPK by metformin improves mitochondrial respiration and hyperglycemia in obesity
evidence.explanation: Metformin activates AMPK (whose α1 catalytic subunit is encoded by PRKAA1/UniProt:Q13131) in hepatocytes and in vivo, demonstrated by knockout of AMPKα1/2 abolishing metformin's glucose-lowering effect.

paper.title: Metformin Improves Mitochondrial Respiratory Activity through Activation of AMPK.

evidence.snippet: raise cytosolic AMP and activate AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK)
evidence.explanation: Comprehensive review confirming that metformin raises cytosolic AMP, which activates AMPK (including the PRKAA1-containing heterotrimeric complex).

paper.title: Metformin: Antidiabetic actions from cells to tissues.

evidence.snippet: activating the hepatic AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) pathway, thus suppressing hepatic gluconeogenesis
evidence.explanation: AMPK activation (via the PRKAA1 catalytic subunit) suppresses hepatic gluconeogenesis, directly supporting the negatively regulates edge.

paper.title: Mechanistic insights of hypoglycemic components from Polygonatum polysaccharide.

evidence.snippet: the main effect of AMPK activation pertinent to the control of hepatic gluconeogenesis is to antagonize glucagon signalling in the short-term
evidence.explanation: Review concludes AMPK activation's primary gluconeogenesis-relevant effect is antagonizing glucagon signalling; supports the directionality but notes the mechanism is indirect (via signalling cross-talk rather than direct transcriptional suppression).

paper.title: AMPK inhibits liver gluconeogenesis: fact or fiction?

evidence.snippet: It counters the effects of insulin resistance, improves glucose homeostasis, assists weight control and avoids overt hypoglycemia via reduced hepatic gluconeogenesis
evidence.explanation: Reducing hepatic gluconeogenesis is a primary means by which metformin avoids hyperglycemia, establishing that elevated gluconeogenesis is positively correlated with hyperglycemia.

paper.title: Metformin: Antidiabetic actions from cells to tissues.

evidence.snippet: PP III administration significantly reduced hyperglycemia while enhancing insulin sensitivity. Transcriptomic sequencing analysis showed that PP III's mechanism involves gut microbiota-mediated short-chain fatty acid production (notably acetic acid and propionic acid), subsequently inhibiting hepatic gluconeogenesis.
evidence.explanation: Inhibiting hepatic gluconeogenesis reduces hyperglycemia in db/db mice, establishing the positive correlation between gluconeogenesis activity and hyperglycemia.

evidence.snippet: Metformin (dimethyl biguanide) is a primary pharmacotherapy to treat hyperglycemia in type 2 diabetes.
evidence.explanation: Hyperglycemia is the defining metabolic manifestation of type 2 diabetes; metformin is prescribed specifically to reduce it.
